51567584.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to His-tagged human p47phox (151 to 386 residues) expressed in Escherichia coli BL21 (DE3) pLysS assessed as dissociation constant by ITC analysis
51567584.references_previous: Reference 84: Grosssoehme, N. E.; Akilesh, S.; Guerinot, M. L.; Wilcox, D. E. Metal-binding thermodynamics of the histidine-rich sequence from the metal-transport protein IRT1 of Arabidopsis thaliana. Inorg. Chem. 2006, 45, 8500–8.

original_paragraph.ITC Measurements: Isothermal Titration Calorimetry (ITC). Calorimetry experiments were performed using an ITC200 microcalorimeter (Malvern Panalytical, MA, U.S.A.). Reference power was 5 μcal/s, injection duration 4 s, injection interval 180 s, stirring speed 600 rpm, and temperature 25 °C. Protein and compounds were solubilized in HBS buffer supplemented with 2% v/v DMSO (25 mM HEPES, 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM TCEP, 7.5, 2% DMSO). A 250 μM solution of His-tagged compound 10 or 33 was titrated into a 250 μM solution of His-tagged p47phoxSH3A-B by 24 × 1.5 or 19 × 2 μL injections, respectively. The p22phox149–168 peptide was tested the same way as 10. The 2-aminoquinoline fragment (compound 1) was tested as a 2500 μM solution titrated into 250 μM p47phoxSH3A-B by 19 × 2 μL injections. Due to the low affinity of 1, three injection schemes were conducted successively without washing the sample cell but removal of excess volume in between. The three individual raw data sets were concatenated to generate a complete titration profile with the aid of the MicroCal Concat ITC V1.00 software.84 All experiments started with an initial control injection of 0.4 μL test compound lasting for 0.8 s, which was excluded prior to data analysis. Heats of dilution were determined by titrating the ligand into buffer and buffer into protein, respectively, and were found negligible and hence not subtracted from the observed heat values of ligand into protein. To rule out artificial buffer signals, pH of all ligand and protein samples was checked and adjusted to match within 0.05 pH unit. Compound concentrations were validated by qNMR.85 UV absorbance at 280 nm using a NanoDrop instrument was used to determine the protein’s stock concentration based on a molar extinction coefficient of 35 050 M−1 cm−1 determined by a prior amino acid analysis externally conducted by Alphalyse A/S (Odense, Denmark). However, this molar extinction coefficient was very close to the one theoretically obtained by the Pace equation (ε280 nm = 37 930 M−1 cm−1). The program Microcal Origin 7.0 (Malvern Panalytical) was used for data processing. Manual baseline correction was performed in case of artificial peaks due to air bubbles. The detected compensation power signals (μcal/s) were integrated to obtain the heat values, which were normalized to kilocalories per mole (kcal/mol) of injected ligand and plotted against the molar ratio of ligand to p47phoxSH3A-B thereby generating the final ITC thermograms. Data were fitted to a one-site model using nonlinear least-squares fitting to determine the thermodynamic properties and stoichiometry of ligand binding. Values are presented as the averages of several individual experiments (n = 2, 12, and 5 for compound 1, 10, 33, and p22phox149–168, respectively).
original_paragraph.Figure 3 caption: Figure 3. Characterization of the direct binding to p47phoxSH3A-B by SPR and ITC. (A) Representative SPR sensorgrams (left) of compound 10 and 33 injected in 2-fold serial dilutions over immobilized p47phoxSH3A-B, and plots of equilibrium binding responses (right) at the end of the analyte injections against the tested concentrations. Sensorgrams are blank injection and reference surface subtracted. The sensorgrams were globally fitted to a 1:1 kinetic interaction model (red lines) to determine the kon and koff rate constants and thereby calculate the “kinetic” Kd values (Table 9). The equilibrium binding responses were also fitted to a one-site binding model to determine the steady-state Kd values (Table 9). (B) Representative ITC thermograms showing binding of compound 10 and 33 to p47phoxSH3A-B. The compounds (250 μM) were titrated into p47phoxSH3A-B (25 μM) in 19 × 2 μL or 24 × 1.5 μL injections. The red line indicates fitting to a one-site binding model.

Binding affinities of monomers 1, 1a, and 1b (Table S1); SAXS derived parameters (Table S2); CRYSOl fits to the SAXS data (Figure S1); OLIGOMER fits to the SAXS data (Figures S2); analytical SEC data (Figure S4); alignment of the published structures of p47phoxSH3A-B in complex with p22phox peptides (Figure S4); ROS scavenging effect of bivalent compounds (Figure S5); relationship between cytotoxicity, NOX2 inhibitory activity, and binding affinity (Figure S6); LCMS traces (UV254) of key compounds (Figure S7); and 1H and 13C NMR spectra of key compounds (Figure S8) (PDF) Molecular formula strings (CSV)
